nodes.label: NOX FiveM Web UI Patterns Reference
NOXES motion guidelines
nodes.rationale: Animation must stay quiet and brief, respect reduced-motion preferences, and never be the only way essential copy is revealed.

nodes.label: AI never writes files directly (core safety invariant)
nodes.rationale: The AI is never trusted to write server files; it stages Change records that a human approves, with a git checkpoint before apply and rollback support.

nodes.label: Change approval / apply pipeline
nodes.rationale: The apply chain is fail-closed: no checkpoint sha means no apply, so every change has a rollback point and an AuditLog entry.

nodes.label: Named Cloudflare tunnel for production
nodes.rationale: Quick tunnel URLs change on every restart; a named tunnel with a custom domain provides a stable production URL.

nodes.label: Build what comes next launch campaign
Suggested launch rollout
nodes.rationale: Publish each project only when there is real work to show, and confirm live URLs and handles before any public post.

nodes.label: Improved Lua manifest parser
nodes.rationale: Regex bugs and unsupported dependency formats caused missed dependencies, so the parser was rewritten with comment removal, multiple dependency formats, table-style deps and deduplication.

nodes.label: updateTheme()
nodes.rationale: Syncs the root element's 'dark' class with the OS prefers-color-scheme setting so the desktop app shell matches the system theme.

nodes.label: Server Detail Page
nodes.rationale: Clicking a server card currently opens a blank page; this is the biggest UX gap and a top quick win (~1 hour). Would host chat/changes/resources/settings/console tabs.

nodes.label: Landing Page Additional Sections
nodes.rationale: Current landing page (Hero -> 3 features -> Security -> Footer) is too short; add pricing, how-it-works, testimonials, FAQ, and CTA sections.

nodes.label: Resources Page (ResourceCatalog)
nodes.rationale: Mirror the desktop app's Resource Finder: 50+ curated FiveM resources with search, category filter, ask-AI-to-install, and download links.

nodes.label: Players Page (PlayerList)
nodes.rationale: Mirror the desktop app's Player Management: online players list, search/filter, ban/unban with reason, and player details modal.

nodes.label: Changes Page (ChangePreview)
nodes.rationale: Enhanced version of the desktop Changes tab: timeline view, diff preview, approve/deny all, and rollback history.

nodes.label: Mobile Responsiveness
nodes.rationale: The Sidebar doesn't collapse on mobile; add a hamburger menu, collapsible sidebar, and touch-friendly buttons.

nodes.label: Dark/Light Mode Toggle
nodes.rationale: Currently hardcoded dark mode; add a settings toggle persisted in localStorage and respecting prefers-color-scheme.

nodes.label: 4-D Method (Deconstruct, Diagnose, Develop, Deliver)
nodes.rationale: The core prompt-optimization workflow: separate confirmed facts from assumptions, surface ambiguity and risks, choose techniques by task type, then deliver with validation. Goal is precision and reliability, not length.

nodes.label: Documentation Rules
nodes.rationale: Consult LYRA_DOC_CATALOG.md for categories and templates; select files by real need, label priority, avoid duplication, keep root agent files under ~150 lines.

nodes.label: Brand Promise
nodes.rationale: Make complex systems easier to shape while keeping people in control. The name has no invented historical or Latin origin; meaning derives from this mission and the product truth of reading resources, staging a diff, asking review, and keeping a recovery checkpoint.

nodes.label: Brand Architecture
nodes.rationale: NOXES is the enduring parent identity; the first product is 'NOXES for FiveM'; future products get their own names endorsed by NOXES. Identity must not rely on FiveM imagery and must not imply an unannounced roadmap.

nodes.label: Warm Signal Palette
nodes.rationale: Replace cobalt and lime: graphite #1D1F20, warm white #F4F0E8, deep ember #B7472F (light surfaces), brighter ember #F28A62 (dark surfaces). Avoid generic neon gradients and stock AI/gaming motifs; keep status colors independent and verify contrast before applying tokens.

nodes.label: Controlled Passage (recommended symbol route)
nodes.rationale: Several separate inputs resolve through one deliberate opening into a clear route; complexity becomes actionable while a person controls the transition. Recommended because it is broad enough for every future product. See concept-01-passage.svg.

nodes.label: Human Checkpoint (symbol route)
nodes.rationale: A continuous route changes direction at a distinct control point before proceeding; expresses the human review that precedes a consequential change. See concept-02-checkpoint.svg.

nodes.label: Recoverable Change (symbol route)
nodes.rationale: A path connects a before-state and an after-state around a stable return point; expresses confidence to make changes because recovery remains possible. See concept-03-return-path.svg.

nodes.label: 01 — Controlled Passage
nodes.rationale: Recommended route: separate inputs resolve through one deliberate opening into a clear route (complexity made actionable under human control). Strength: broad enough for every future product. Test: keep it from reading like a flowchart or a letter.

nodes.label: 02 — Human Checkpoint
nodes.rationale: A route changes direction at a distinct control point before continuing; consequential actions remain a human decision. Strength: expresses review and agency. Test: avoid resembling a generic routing/navigation icon.

nodes.label: 03 — Recoverable Change
nodes.rationale: Two states remain connected by a clear return path; builders can move forward with confidence and recover when needed. Strength: grounded in checkpoints and rollback. Test: avoid looking like a generic undo or infinity symbol.

nodes.label: Persistent Storage (data/projects.json)
nodes.rationale: Projects are stored in data/projects.json for easy editing; public GET API is read-only while the admin API holds full CRUD behind a Clerk session check.

nodes.label: Path safety duplication (is_path_safe vs validatePath)
nodes.rationale: Tauri (is_path_safe: canonicalization + depth counting) and the Node agent (validatePath: path.resolve/startsWith) implement path safety independently. Both solve the same problem with different algorithms and no shared utility: maintenance burden x2, drift risk, no single source of truth. HIGH severity.

nodes.label: NODE_ENV direct read vs config.nodeEnv
nodes.rationale: authAllowAnon() reads process.env.NODE_ENV directly even though config already parses/exports nodeEnv; two reads of the same var can silently diverge. Should import config.nodeEnv.

nodes.label: JWT_SECRET validation duplication (IIFE vs zod)
nodes.rationale: configSchema defines jwtSecret: z.string().min(32) and a runtime IIFE re-checks length < 32, with schema validation running again in production. Same rule encoded twice; validate once via schema.

nodes.label: ensure_scoped duplicate '..' check
nodes.rationale: ensure_scoped rejects '..' segments before calling is_path_safe, which again counts '..' in the missing tail; the same traversal check runs twice. HIGH severity.

nodes.label: AUTH_ALLOW_ANON flag
nodes.rationale: Defaults to true so existing deploys keep working: headerless requests are treated as an anonymous user bound to legacy dev-org, while invalid/expired tokens still get 401. Flip to false only after the updated web and desktop builds are deployed; rollback is just flipping back to true.

nodes.label: AGENT_LEGACY_OK flag
nodes.rationale: When true, a tokenless agent WS hello is accepted only if the device's stored pairingTokenHash is NULL (paired before tokens existed). Flipping to false requires every device to have a hash and a matching session token.

nodes.label: Legacy dev-org tenant
nodes.rationale: Orphaned tenant that anonymous callers write into while AUTH_ALLOW_ANON=true; no real customer data is reachable because every Clerk-authenticated caller gets their own org, but anonymous writes are not blocked.

nodes.label: Frozen Node CLI agent (apps/agent)
nodes.rationale: CLI is frozen and never persists or sends session tokens, so new pairings are dead once a claim stores a hash (tokenless hello gets INVALID_TOKEN). Treat the CLI as EOL for new pairings and direct users to the desktop installer; ops SQL can null hashes to extend existing devices.

nodes.label: Dependency Vulnerabilities (vitest, tar, fastify, next)
nodes.rationale: pnpm audit revealed 52 vulnerabilities (3 critical, 24 high, 21 moderate, 4 low): vitest RCE, tar DoS/file overwrite, fastify DoS, next.js DoS/XSS. MUST FIX IMMEDIATELY.

nodes.label: Hardcoded JWT Secret fallback
nodes.rationale: apps/orchestrator/src/config/index.ts falls back to 'dev-secret-change-in-production-min-32-chars' in production, enabling authentication bypass and session hijacking. Remove the fallback and require JWT_SECRET.

nodes.label: Missing Rate Limiting on Agent Endpoints
Insecure WebSocket Authentication (timing attack)
nodes.rationale: agentGateway.ts legacy-mode session token verification uses a non-constant-time SHA-256 compare; use crypto.timingSafeEqual for all token comparisons.

nodes.label: Missing Input Sanitization in Chat Service
Cloudflare Quick Tunnels (ephemeral)
nodes.rationale: Quick Tunnels are ephemeral and get a new random URL on every restart, so tunnel manager restarts may require env updates; NEXT_PUBLIC_ORCHESTRATOR_URL is already the stable /api/orchestrator proxy.

nodes.label: Docker Compose OmniRoute Service
nodes.rationale: Production-preferred option: run OmniRoute and cloudflared as services in vps/docker-compose.yml so the tunnel is managed on the VPS rather than manually on a PC.

nodes.label: AI chat 'Response received.' issue
nodes.rationale: The AI chat shows only 'Response received.' because OmniRoute isn't connected; fix by starting OmniRoute plus a cloudflared tunnel and updating NEXT_PUBLIC_OMNIROUTE_URL, or running OmniRoute on the VPS.

nodes.label: Controlled Passage brand mark (concept 01)
nodes.rationale: 256x256 monoline logo mark. Three routes enter from the left (straight middle route plus top and bottom routes that curve inward) and converge at a single central point (121,128), then continue as one clear horizontal path ending in a solid dark terminus dot on the right. Two short vertical strokes at x=151 form a deliberate gate/opening that the merged path passes through. Near-black #1D1F20 stroke, width 14, rounded caps and joins.

nodes.label: Controlled Passage
nodes.rationale: Three routes converge and pass through a deliberate opening into one clear path. Design intent: express consolidation of multiple inputs through a controlled gate into a single unambiguous output, a brand metaphor for managed, gated access.

nodes.label: Human Checkpoint brand mark (concept 02)
nodes.rationale: 256x256 monoline logo mark. A single route starts bottom-left, travels right, bends upward, then turns right again toward a dark terminus dot at top-right, forming a stepped S-shaped path. A rust-red accent circle (#B7472F) at (128,151) marks the bend, the deliberate checkpoint where the route changes direction. Near-black #1D1F20 stroke, width 15, rounded caps and joins.

nodes.label: Human Checkpoint
nodes.rationale: A route changes direction at a deliberate point before proceeding. Design intent: mark a human decision or oversight point within an otherwise continuous flow; the rust-red dot visually highlights the intentional intervention.

nodes.label: Recoverable Change brand mark (concept 03)
nodes.rationale: 256x256 monoline logo mark. Two parallel horizontal routes (top at y=79, bottom at y=178) joined at the right by a U-shaped loop, forming a closed circuit. The left ends carry arrowhead chevrons pointing back to the left. A rust-red accent circle (#B7472F) on the top route at (147,79) and a near-black circle on the bottom route at (147,178) mark two linked states. Near-black #1D1F20 stroke, width 14, rounded caps and joins.

nodes.label: Recoverable Change
nodes.rationale: A stable checkpoint links two states with a clear return route. Design intent: express reversibility, showing that a change can be made and then returned from, with arrowheads indicating the way back to a stable state.

nodes.label: Noxes identity-v2 shared visual language
nodes.rationale: All three concept marks share a 256x256 viewBox, a near-black #1D1F20 monoline stroke (width 14-15) with rounded caps and joins, solid dark terminus dots, a route/path metaphor, and a rust-red #B7472F accent circle marking a deliberate control point (used in concepts 02 and 03). This shared grammar presents the marks as one coherent brand system.
